worktreeAt/describeWorktree in the new takeOver/removeLeftover code duplicates the existing registeredWorktree() helper (same listWorktrees+canonical matching logic), just returning the object instead of a boolean. Minor duplication, not a defect.
items.resolution_reason: Minor code duplication, not a defect

items.summary: If the process dies before verify's/run's normal cleanup runs (e.g. the documented second-SIGINT immediate exit, or an uncaught crash), tmp.mjs's exit handler removes the harness-base-* directory from disk via fs.rmSync but does not run `git worktree remove`, so the repository's .git/worktrees/<name> registration can be left pointing at a now-missing directory. AC-4's checks only look for leftover directories under os.tmpdir(), which are indeed gone, so this doesn't fail any criterion, and the SPEC text for the second-SIGINT case only promises the temporary path is removed, not worktree deregistration.
items.resolution_reason: Only after crash/second SIGINT; stale .git/worktrees entry is pruned by git worktree prune

items.summary: takeOver's carried-work commit runs `git add -A` over everything the earlier builder left untracked, including files such as .env or local credentials. That work is then merged into integration. This matches how the core already commits builder changes, but a secret_globs exclusion on the carried-work commit would make it harder to commit a secret by accident.
items.resolution_reason: Consistent with how the core commits all builder changes; builder cooperative

items.summary: Takeover refuses a worktree only when MERGE_HEAD is present. A leftover worktree in the middle of a rebase, cherry-pick or revert (REBASE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, detached rebase state) is either taken over and committed as carried work, or blocked only indirectly through the detached-HEAD check. The contract does not name these states.
items.resolution_reason: Rebase/cherry-pick states in a harness worktree need non-cooperative builder actions (D1); rare

items.summary: worktreeAt compares paths after realpath. If .harness/wt/F{n} is a symlink to another registered worktree that is on harness/F{n}, the symlink passes the SC-1 check. This needs deliberate filesystem manipulation, so it is outside threat model D1.
items.resolution_reason: Needs deliberate filesystem manipulation (D1)

items.summary: state.fresh is saved in the run state, so a --resume of a run that stopped at stage 'worktree' still removes the leftover worktree and branch for those features. This is consistent with the user's original --fresh intent, but SPEC §8 does not say so.
items.resolution_reason: Behaviour matches user intent; SPEC wording nit

items.summary: lib/run.mjs's hooksOff() still uses one core.hooksPath directory per process (created once via makeTempDir, reused across the run, removed at process exit) rather than per git call. It's a unique mkdtemp path (not the shared literal 'harness-no-hooks-dir' B29 described), so it isn't the same bug, and AC-2 explicitly scopes the per-call requirement to verify/eval only — but it's worth aligning with the same per-call pattern for consistency.
items.resolution_reason: Consistency-only: hooksOff() uses a unique mkdtemp dir per process, never populated, removed at exit; no hook can run. AC scoped per-call to verify/eval only. (evidence: lib/run.mjs:120-131)

items.summary: The base vacuity check runs with a live symlink/junction to the working tree's node_modules, so a base-side check that writes under node_modules (e.g. node_modules/.cache from babel/jest/vite) modifies the working tree's node_modules. SC-1 only covers the harness's own link handling; consider documenting this or linking read-only where possible.
items.resolution_reason: Writes of tool caches (node_modules/.cache) through the base link are benign and cooperative-builder (D1); the link is documented as deliberate (§6.3). (evidence: lib/verify.mjs:436-452)

items.summary: In ensureOverlaidBase, newOnBase is computed with fs.lstatSync(path.join(dir, f)) after the node_modules link exists. For an overlay path under node_modules/ this resolves through the link into the working tree, so a feature-created file there is wrongly treated as present on base (affects only entry-script withholding for files under node_modules).
items.resolution_reason: Still true (link made in addBaseWorktree before the lstat in ensureOverlaidBase), but only affects feature-created entry scripts committed under node_modules/, which is practically never tracked. (evidence: lib/verify.mjs:465,484-487)

items.summary: commandPrograms splits only on '&&', '||', ';', '|' (per contract). A newline-separated multi-line check (e.g. 'cd sub\njest') still judges only the first program, so a missing later program remains a plain exit-127 failure.
items.resolution_reason: Still true (no '\n' split), but multi-line checks are rare and the consequence is only exit-127 reported as a plain failure instead of 'command not found'; the check still fails. (evidence: lib/exec.mjs:138-162)

items.summary: Windows junction cleanup relies on fs.lstatSync(link).isSymbolicLink() being true for junctions and on fs.rmSync/git worktree remove not descending into junctions; the SC-1/ES-1 behaviour is only exercised on POSIX in this review (tests use symlinks on macOS).
items.resolution_reason: Windows-only coverage gap with no demonstrated user-facing defect. (evidence: lib/verify.mjs:446,642)

items.summary: The AC-2 integration test (runFeatures with a custom `build` stub) bypasses defaultBuild's redact wiring and calls adapter.run() without the run's own SR-8 redact function, falling back to common.mjs's default `redactor(process.env)`. This still exercises the observable AC-2 behavior but doesn't directly verify that `redact` is correctly threaded from runFeatures into defaultBuild for the postMergeFailures build path.
items.resolution_reason: Test-style preference; observable AC-2 behavior is exercised. (evidence: test/f48-merge-robustness.test.mjs)

items.summary: In `harness run`, a second SIGTERM/SIGHUP calls process.exit(130) at once. If it arrives before the abort from the first signal has finished killing the detached step group, builder descendants could outlive the harness. SC-1 only covers a single signal. Consider killing the active groups synchronously before process.exit.
items.resolution_reason: Defect does not exist on POSIX: controller.abort() fires the 'abort' listener synchronously, and killTree SIGKILLs the process group synchronously, so the groups are dead before a second signal can be handled. Windows does not deliver SIGTERM (exec.mjs:25). (evidence: lib/commands/run.mjs:59-64; lib/exec.mjs:32-40,90-92)

items.summary: runAdapter redacts stderr/stdout only on the exit_nonzero path. The `parsed` fields spread into every result (the stdout text of the CLI) are not redacted in memory. They are redacted later on the SR-8 write paths, but any new consumer that embeds them mid-string before a cut would bring back the B268 pattern.
items.resolution_reason: Hypothetical future consumer; all current write paths redact (SR-8). (evidence: lib/adapters/common.mjs:171-186)

items.summary: Outside run and eval, the fallback redactor(process.env) has no env_allowlist. Allowlisted values of 8 or more characters (for example a project-specific variable the user allowlisted) get redacted in adapter error details there, which makes those diagnostics less useful. This matches the SPEC wording but differs from the run/eval redaction.
items.resolution_reason: Matches SPEC by design; over-redaction in diagnostics is safe-side. (evidence: lib/adapters/common.mjs)

items.summary: In runFeatures' skipped-dependent handling (lib/run.mjs:1508), the recorded `tier` for a skipped feature's result entry still comes straight from features.json (`f.security_tier`) rather than `effectiveTier(root, f).tier`. It's purely informational display for a feature that never started (not used for any preflight/critical-stop decision), so it doesn't affect AC-1..4/SC-1/ES-1, but it's an inconsistency with the rest of the diff's 'contract tier wins' rule.
items.resolution_reason: Still true but informational only; the report table does not even print tier. (evidence: lib/run.mjs:1526,601)

items.summary: cleanIntegration() resets and cleans any dirt in the integration worktree (.harness/wt/_integration) before a merge, not only what a post-merge verify left. Before this change, a dirty integration worktree stopped the run with 'clean it before running'. Now, manual edits a user made there between runs (for example before --resume) are silently discarded by `git reset --hard` / `git clean -fd`. The SPEC wording names only verify leftovers. Consider logging the discarded paths, or cleaning only after a merge this run made.

state.warnings accumulates the security_tier mismatch warning each time a feature starts. A resumed run (or a retried feature) can append the same warning again, so the report's '## Warnings' section may list duplicates. Consider de-duplicating.

items.summary: The new 절대 regex /절대(로)?(?=\s|$)(?!\s*경로)/ also exempts '절대로 경로…' (e.g. '절대로 경로를 바꾸지 않는다'), which is a real universal negation and not the technical term '절대 경로'. Consider exempting only '절대' + optional whitespace + '경로', not '절대로'.

redactDeep keeps object keys unredacted, so event data only stays clean while its keys come from trusted identifiers. Today plan/approve `criteria` is keyed by criterion ids, and approve refuses contracts whose ids fail the AC-n/SC-n/ES-n lint, so no secret gets through. A future event that uses free text or environment-derived strings as keys would bypass redaction.

Only `data` is redacted. The top-level `feature` and `type` fields are written as given. Current callers pass validated F<n> ids and constant type names, but recordEvent does not enforce this, so a later F55+ caller could leak free text there.

`harness events` prints stored lines exactly as they are in the file. It does not redact again on read, so a line written by another tool, or before env_allowlist or secrets changed, is shown unmodified.

Event redaction relies on process.env at write time, like the run report. A secret that is not an environment variable of the process (for example, one typed directly into a contract) is written in plain text. This is the same rule as SR-8, so the contract accepts it.

repro_program has no documented or enforced length cap: cmdName() returns the raw last path segment of the first token verbatim, so a repro whose first word is a very long string with no path separator lands in the event unbounded, unlike criterion_id/dimension/summary/problems which all have a stated cut length.

harness decide's backlog item (kind: decision) is added without a `summary` field and never gets `resolved_by` set (resolveItems only resolves ids listed in a later contract's `resolves` array). Since openItems/backlogSection (lib/eval.mjs:437-447) render `i.summary ?? ''`, every future eval prompt's '## Open backlog' section — and `harness status`'s open-item count — will permanently show a blank '- Bn [-] ' line for each decision, for the life of the project. Confirmed via `openItems({items:[{id:'B1',kind:'decision',...}]})` returning the item with no summary and no way to close it.

harness note [F<n>] does not validate that F<n> exists in features.json (unlike harness decide, which does), so a typo'd feature id is recorded silently. The contract only says the feature is optional, not that it must be known, so this is a minor asymmetry rather than a spec violation.

lib/metrics.mjs and lib/usage.mjs each define an identical local `finite` helper (`(v) => typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v) ? v : null`); minor duplication introduced by this diff, though sharing it would create a circular import (metrics.mjs already imports usage.mjs).

verify/command `program` is path.basename(firstProgram(cmd)). firstProgram only skips leading NAME=value words while at least one more word follows, so a verify command made of a single assignment (e.g. `TOKEN=abc123`) records `TOKEN=abc123` as the program. That value is a literal in config.json, not an environment variable, so the SR-8 redactor does not mask it. This is an unusual config and the same config file already holds the value, but the event file may later be exported (F57). Consider recording null when the first word is an assignment.

`session_log.path` records the absolute home directory and the real working-directory path (which contains the username) in events. SPEC §2 documents this and it is not a secret, but it is identifying information once events are exported to a hub (F57). Worth considering hashing or making it relative to home at export time.

The eval/security step event also passes the evaluator's cRound field through the `...c` spread into stepEventData. stepEventData drops unknown keys, so nothing leaks today. The allow-list depends on stepEventData's destructuring staying exhaustive, and no test pins its exact key set the way METRIC_FIELDS pins the metrics line.

No test covers the critical + security_tier path where the evaluator's own reply fails schema validation twice (eval_error via evalErr(ev)) while the security-reviewer's reply succeeds normally. In that branch, security/finding events from the successful reviewer run are flushed without an `unused: true` marker, and security/verdict.reviewer reads 'unused' rather than reflecting that the whole evaluation ended in eval_error — consistent with the literal SPEC §7.8 text (which scopes the `unused: true` rule to the §7.4 'evaluator has a blocking finding' case only) but unverified by any AC-1/AC-3 test.

When the evaluator returns eval_error on a critical feature, the security-reviewer's security/finding events are still flushed, but they do not get `unused: true`. SPEC §7.8 only calls for that flag on the §7.4 unused path. The error path still leaves them looking like findings that counted toward a verdict.
lib/telemetry.mjs defines its own sha16 helper identical to the one already in lib/events.mjs, instead of importing it — minor duplication introduced by this diff.

writeExport uses fs.writeFileSync(plan.file, text, {flag:'wx'}) keyed by a millisecond-resolution timestamp; two exports for the same project completing within the same millisecond (e.g. concurrent `harness eval` invocations with auto_export on) would collide and the second would fail with EEXIST, surfaced as an export failure rather than a merged/renamed bundle. Not covered by any ES criterion and outside the single-process test scenarios exercised.

The project id is an unsalted sha256 prefix of the absolute repository path. Paths are low-entropy (for example /Users/<name>/Project/<repo>), so anyone who holds the hub bundle and guesses candidate paths can recover the user name and repository name by dictionary search. The contract accepts a path hash, but a per-install salt or a random project id stored in .harness would make it non-reversible.

Test names are exported as unsalted sha256 prefixes. Well-known or guessable test names (for example from a public repository) can be confirmed by hashing candidates. This is within the contract, but a salted hash would remove the linkage.

Status-event reasons that are not backlog reasons are dropped from the export because data.reason only accepts backlog-reason values. Examples are 'approve', 'run_start', 'dependency_blocked', and eval verdicts such as 'pass'/'fail'. Aggregating status transitions across projects loses this signal. It is not a security issue.

Events can be lost in two cases. First, runExport fixes `now` before readEvents runs, and the next export starts at that `now`. An event another process (for example a parallel run) appends with ts < now after the read is never exported. Second, if .harness/events/.exported holds a time in the future (clock skew), every later export reports nothing until the clock passes it.

The hub directory and bundle files are created with the default umask (usually world-readable 0644/0755) under ~/.cc-harness/hub. The data is anonymized, but restricting the hub to 0700/0600 would be a safer default for a directory meant to collect data from many projects.

reproProgram lowercases the program name before the event is redacted at write time. If a repro's first word is itself a secret environment value that contains uppercase letters (for example `$ABC_TOKEN_VALUE arg` written out as a literal), the lowercased form no longer matches the redactor's exact value. The lowercased secret is then stored in repro_program. To reproduce, the evaluator has to put a literal secret in the program position. A fix would be to redact before cmdName lowercases, or to apply clip() to repro_program.

evalErr flushes eval/verdict and security/verdict events after finishError has written the eval_error file. A concurrent evaluation of the same round writes these events twice. Nothing deduplicates by round the way refuseExisting does for pass/fail verdicts.

Not covered by any frozen criterion's check (ES-1's loop never combines --json with --compare) and ES-1's literal text ('출력하고 exit 0') is still satisfied, so this doesn't block, but it's a real doc/behavior gap worth a backlog note.

F59's own test suite (test/f59-learn.test.mjs) is thorough, but resume-safety of the new per-feature build-total aggregation (lib/run.mjs addBuildTotals, e.build) across a process restart (`harness run --resume`) isn't directly exercised — only a single in-process two-round run is tested. Reading the surrounding code, e.build is mutated on the same object held in state.active and persisted by save() after each step, so it appears resume-safe by inspection, but no test pins this.

A re-approval with an unchanged contract keeps the hash, so the round count continues past max_rounds: interactive eval ran and passed 'contract round 4/3' without any notice. Decide whether a same-hash re-approval resets rounds (human override) or eval refuses past max_rounds, and show the override explicitly.

lib/telemetry.mjs still exports `lastExport(root)`, but after this diff nothing in lib/, bin/, or test/ calls it — planExport now uses readExported directly. It was the primary function before this change (used internally by the old planExport) and is now orphaned dead code.

Adding USERNAME/USERDOMAIN/COMPUTERNAME/HOSTNAME/LOGONSERVER to BASE_ENV_ALLOWLIST also widens filteredEnv, so check/repro child processes now receive these user and host names. They are not secrets, and SR-2 now documents them, but this is a small increase in what untrusted repro commands can see.

readNewEvents reads each event file fully into memory on every export (fs.readFileSync of the whole YYYY-MM.jsonl), even when only a small tail after the recorded position is new. This is fine at the current scale, but a positioned read from `start` would bound memory and I/O.

The '## Language' section is duplicated near-verbatim across 11 files (AGENTS.md, 7 skills, 3 agents). This is required by AC-1's per-file test, but it means any future wording tweak has to be repeated 11 times by hand with no shared source.

test/f60-field-accuracy.test.mjs's timeout values (8000ms/1s -> 12000ms/5s) were changed in this diff for load stability, unrelated to F61's language feature; a reasonable bundled fix but outside this contract's scope.

init.mjs's --language validation uses HarnessError code 'usage' for a missing value versus 'config_invalid' for a malformed one; consistent with existing CLI conventions but worth confirming both map to exit 2 as tested.
CC_HARNESS_TELEMETRY 는 정확히 '0' 또는 'off' 일 때만 끈다. 'OFF'·'false'·'no'·' 0' 은 config 를 따르므로, 끄려던 사용자가 이 값을 쓰면 텔레메트리가 켜진 채로 남는다. 계약대로의 동작이지만, 기본값이 켜짐으로 바뀐 만큼 대소문자를 가리지 않고 받거나 알 수 없는 값에 경고를 내면 더 안전하다.
run 과 eval 은 autoExport 를 호출할 때 env 를 넘기지 않아 process.env 를 쓴다. 두 명령이 in-process 로 다른 env 를 받는 경우(테스트나 앞으로의 호출자)에 CC_HARNESS_TELEMETRY 판단과 허브 경로가 그 env 가 아니라 프로세스의 env 를 따른다. 지금 CLI 경로에서는 결과가 같다.

init.mjs's action→word map conflates 'inserted' and 'updated' into the same displayed text ('updated'), so the CLI message can't distinguish 'block added after the first heading' from 'existing block rewritten'; no criterion checks this distinction so it's harmless but slightly confusing.

blockStatus/harness claude-md --check compares the block's version marker to package.json's version with exact string equality, so every core patch release marks every project's block 'outdated' even when templates/claude-block.md content is unchanged, prompting a rewrite nag on each release. This matches the literal SPEC text (version compared, not content) so it's not a defect, just a design note for future consideration.

applyBlock's fallback title for a brand-new CLAUDE.md is `path.basename(path.resolve(root))` inserted verbatim as a Markdown heading (lib/claudemd.mjs:110/152). A project directory literally named with '#', backslashes, or other Markdown-significant characters would produce a slightly malformed heading. No criterion covers directory-name content, so this is a minor edge case rather than a defect.

SPEC §4.1 says `harness init` warns and continues when the block can't be written (a symbolic-link CLAUDE.md or malformed markers), and init.mjs implements this (lib/commands/init.mjs catches HarnessError and calls err(...)), but no F62 test exercises `harness init` against a symlinked or malformed CLAUDE.md to confirm the rest of init still completes and the warning is printed.
